claim_types.description: The VEX justification of an agent's app-level not_affected judgment: why this inventory's use of the component is not affected. It silences this occurrence only and never states the global none. A justification is the not_affected judgment; beside a verdict of affected it is no judgment.
The occurrence (one inventory's component) judged; a key part.
A codebase fact this judgment was made in light of. Core does not act on it: when the fact changes, run the resting_on Query for it. Never settled by a Mandate.

An agent's verdict on this inventory's exposure. affected stands alone, with no justification, and cites the reachability evidence (the code that reaches the vulnerable function). not_affected goes with a justification, which alone also means not_affected. A verdict of affected beside a justification is no judgment: the pair stays in the worklists. Never settled by a Mandate.

member_descriptions.description: The vulnerable code is reachable here: remediate or escalate. No justification.
Not reachable here, for the reason the pair's justification states.

claim_types.description: The vulnerability judged; a key part.
The catalog's short id, e.g. cisa-kev; the catalog's key.
What sort of fact it is. Cites the notes section stating the fact, where it holds and its known exceptions. Never settled by a Mandate.

member_descriptions.description: Where untrusted input enters or trust changes.
A dangerous helper or sink whose callers need checking.

claim_types.description: Whether the fact holds in the code, citing the passage that decides it (path#anchor); it drifts when that passage changes. Never settled by a Mandate.

member_descriptions.description: Does not hold: the code contradicts it.
Holds, with exceptions the notes name.
Holds wherever the notes say it applies.

claim_types.description: The repository as host/owner/repo, casefolded (as a finding's repo); with topic, the fact's key.
What the fact is about, as a short stable slug in the agent's words (authn-middleware, sql-parameterisation, tenant-id-source), spelled the same every run; with repo, the fact's key.

A vulnerability OSV lists for the component's exact purl@version (OSV's own version matching). None of V is an agent's package-level not_affected judgment (normative, own words), which OSV cannot override.
The component's package URL with its version (qualifiers dropped); the component's key.
What the surface was checked for, in the auditor's words or a reference attack class (access-control, injection, ssrf, a named state machine); with repo and surface, the unit's key.
The repository as host/owner/repo, casefolded (as a finding's repo); with surface and concern, the unit's key.
A codebase fact this judgment was made in light of. Core does not act on it: when the fact changes, run the resting_on Query for it. Never settled by a Mandate.
What an audit agent did with the unit, in its own words or citing the examined passage. Never settled by a Mandate.

member_descriptions.description: Stopped: a missing sandbox capability or a fact outside source, named in the rationale.
Examined; the Claim cites the exact passage (path#anchor).

claim_types.description: The entry point or boundary checked, as a canonical code reference: path#symbol, or a route (src/router.ts#POST /users/:id). Spelled the same every run; with repo and concern, the unit's key.
The component (package release) judged; a key part.

The VEX justification of an agent's package-level not_affected judgment, stated with affected_by none of the vulnerability on the component: the vulnerable code is not in this package release, for every inventory.
The vulnerability judged; a key part.
The commit (40-hex SHA) that fixes the finding, as an agent states it.
The coverage unit an audit agent was working when it found the finding. Never settled by a Mandate.
Why a finding is false_positive or not_exploitable, as an agent judged it.

member_descriptions.description: The effect stays within the attacker's own authority.

claim_types.description: Where in the code: <path>#<locator>, the first tier that applies (symbol, snippet:<12 hex>, line-hash:<the tool's>). Never a line number; with repo and weakness, the finding's key.
The repository as host/owner/repo, casefolded; with weakness and locus, the finding's key.

Where the finding was reported, as path:line: by the latest scan, or by an audit agent citing the code there. A moved finding keeps its key and this revises; a full scan that no longer reports it retires the scan's.
A finder that reported the finding: a tool (semgrep, codeql) from a SARIF scan, or audit for an audit agent citing the code.
A codebase fact this judgment was made in light of. Core does not act on it: when the fact changes, run the resting_on Query for it. Never settled by a Mandate.
A rule that reported the finding: tool:ruleId from a SARIF scan, or the concern an audit agent was checking.
How severe the finding is: a scan's severity (security-severity, else the level), or an agent's normative judgment, which a later scan never overrides.

An agent's verdict: confirmed (real and exploitable), false_positive (no such weakness here) or not_exploitable (real, but not exploitable here). A confirmed verdict cites the observed run output (a catalogued test log or output file); a refutation cites the agent's own words. Never settled by a Mandate.
present when a scan reports the finding; fixed when a full scan of the rules that reported it no longer does. fixed needs complete input.
CWE-<n>, the smallest CWE the reporting rule names, else RULE:<tool>/<ruleId>; with repo and locus, the finding's key.
What one SBOM describes, named by its metadata.component purl (or, without one, by the SBOM's workspace path); the inventory's key.
The component this occurrence places in its inventory; a key part.
The inventory this occurrence is in; a key part.
The component's CycloneDX scope in this inventory's SBOM (required when the SBOM states none). The membership fact: live while the SBOM lists the component, retired when it no longer does.
The CVE identifier; the vulnerability's key.
The EPSS score's percentile among all scored CVEs (percentile).
FIRST's EPSS probability of exploitation in the next 30 days (epss).
The date FIRST computed the EPSS score and percentile (date).
The date CISA added the vulnerability to the KEV catalog (dateAdded).
The KEV remediation due date for federal agencies (dueDate).
Whether KEV reports known ransomware campaign use (knownRansomwareCampaignUse).
A catalog that lists the vulnerability, from the catalog's own retained document; none of a catalog means a complete read of it did not list it.

source: kits/security/artifacts at kits 84fd3a7 (security 1.3.0): every ClaimType and SubjectKind the kit ships

subject_kinds.description: An (occurrence, vulnerability) pair an agent judged for one inventory, keyed by its ends.
A published vulnerability catalog (e.g. cisa-kev), named by its id.
One thing true of a repository's code that security judgments rest on.
One package release, named by its purl@version (R1, R12).
One audit coverage unit: one surface of one repository checked for one concern.
A (component, vulnerability) pair an agent judged at package level, keyed by its ends.
One weakness of one kind at one place in one repository's code.
What one SBOM describes (an application, an image, an environment).
A component's place in one inventory, keyed by (inventory, component); its scope is the membership fact.
A CVE, named by its id.
